name: Japan Masters
stakes: This week is crucial for India to build momentum and secure vital BWF World Tour ranking points, especially for Lakshya Sen's push towards the season-ending Tour Finals.
summary: India's campaign at the Japan Masters has seen mixed fortunes, with **Lakshya Sen** leading the charge into the semifinals. Fresh off his Hylo Open title, Sen—currently ranked 13th—is making a strong push to break into the top eight of the BWF World Tour rankings, a crucial step for qualifying for the season-ending Tour Finals. His quarterfinal win over Japan's Yushi Tanaka was a confident display, setting him up for a potential deep run. However, it wasn't all smooth sailing for the Indian contingent, as veteran **Kidambi Srikanth** bowed out of the tournament. While the specific round of his exit wasn't detailed, his departure means one less Indian presence in the later stages. Top men's doubles pair **Satwik & Chirag** (seeded 4th, world No. 5) and women's singles star **PV Sindhu** (world No. 6) are still in the hunt, with their draws yet to fully unfold. Rising women's doubles pair **Treesa & Gayatri** and men's singles campaigner **HS Prannoy** are also looking to make their mark, alongside young talent **Malvika Bansod**. This Super 500 event offers valuable points and momentum as the season progresses, with the Tour Finals looming large for many.
